notes.title: Warchief Journal #5
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/b916641144d208fbe4ca7e954bbb2dff2c91438d.png"][/img][/p][p]The art direction is an evolving vision. As we continued to refine the core mechanics, the visuals naturally evolved to better represent the spirit of mindful strategy and Orcish charm. [b]With each milestone, the art becomes a closer reflection of the game’s essence.[/b] Let’s start with the improvements we’ve made to the game’s overall visual identity! [/p][p][/p][h1]Visual Identity[/h1][p]Even though we liked the direction we were going, we felt the art style was missing a bit of punch. That’s why we started tweaking assets, textures, and characters until we found a look that really fit the spirit of the game. The result? Brighter colors, thicker lines, and a style that feels more lively, a little rough around the edges, and unmistakably [i]Don’t Kill Them All.[/i] [/p][list][*][p]Heavy black strokes in line art.[/p][/*][*][p]Brighter, bolder colors.[/p][/*][*][p]Sharper contrast on screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Rough, gritty textures in assets.[/p][/*][*][p]Unique brushes and textures across every element.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/33a9dfa0db2e10970effd5c732a21c2d5a8fc5ec.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/7f61cc6dad1c2c4807ee1a441746ddf8b920f9e1.png"][/img][/p][h1]Characters[/h1][p]After the Kickstarter, our Orcs treated themselves to a little makeover. To align with the game’s evolving art style, they now appear bolder, squarer, and stockier. Orcs are beings of mass destruction, after all![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/08f49719a1783b94dbef2312c83f31032b5a5001.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve been refining the balance between the Orcs' violent yet endearing personalities and their enemies that should look cute yet hostile. The visual contrast between an armored Orc wielding an axe and a deceptively adorable mushroom highlights this direction. It also reinforces the core premise of the game: you probably shouldn’t kill the cute mushrooms… but the Orcs just can’t help themselves.[/p][p][/p][p]For enemies, we’re leaning more and more into a cute-but-creepy style, drawing inspiration from animals, nature and fantastical creatures rather than humanoid designs. Here’s some research for the enemies of our first environment, [i]Fablewood Thickets.[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/16151a75ca2d7d356106c3467c108e31d9c973ca.png"][/img][/p][h1]UI[/h1][p]Our UI style is still taking shape, but we’ve got a clear idea of where it’s headed. Our goal is to keep it clean and highly readable, while staying true to the game’s identity through bold textures, chunky icons, and handcrafted illustrations that carry a playful spirit.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/ddbda1e95ca407e600f7aa8e88f7d6321bd83551.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/556bb0e210ff58b750ba80c072b2d4a6bcab179e.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve also been sketching some iconography, as it’s a great way to visually enrich the world with symbols inspired by Orc clan culture and backstory. Who are the Orcs, and what symbols define them? As you’ll see here, boars have been a big source of inspiration![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/34caf0f02524d42ce68380cbc3526b61f2ad0c9c.png"][/img][/p][p]Overall, our work on the UI is far from finished, and it will be greatly shaped by feedback from everyone who joins the Beta. [/p][p][/p][h1]Environments[/h1][p]Even though the game is tile-based, we’re focusing on making the environments feel organic and alive, preserving the charm of a hand-designed world. Every location, from the Orc camp to the faraway biomes, is crafted to carry its own identity and atmosphere, giving you a world that feels worth exploring.[/p][p] [/p][h2]The Orc camp[/h2][p]The Orc camp is meant to feel a little desolate at first, reflecting that the clan is no longer in its glory days. But in our first iteration, it felt too desolate. Since the camp is your base, the place you’ll return to again and again, it should still feel cozy. A safe haven from the chaos of the raids. To create this atmosphere, we leaned into warmer colors, sprinkled in stylized desert plants, and made sure the Orc spirit was alive in the materials: rough bones, heavy rocks, knotted ropes, and weathered wood.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/600015bc339f6e1b4614047a4331ee5f9af25552.png"][/img][/p][h2]The other biomes,[/h2][p]A big part of DKTA takes place outside the camp, where you’ll raid for resources and discover new environments. The raids will be mostly procedurally generated with the addition of special handcrafted rooms.[/p][p][/p][p]We can’t show much yet, as we’re still crafting the building blocks of the world. Each environment is designed with its own twist and distinctive visual identity. Take [i]Fablewood Thickets[/i] for example: an intriguing lush forest with an eerie yet quirky vibe inspired by dark fairytales. Its palette blends deep teals and purples with glowing orange accents, while its landscape is filled with organic, twisting, and spiralling shapes that bring the forest to life (quite literally).[/p][p][/p][p]But we’re having a blast creating these little worlds, and we can’t wait for you to explore them too![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/6b4b67ec0ab71bf3585c966121613724b6e7631f.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/0439149e96918b6dd2ba236c92919653a84d165f.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Quick note here:[/b] these are concept artworks, not in-game assets. They’re here to spark inspiration, and the final game might look a little different![/p][p][/p][h1]Animation[/h1][p]Orcs don’t waste time thinking, they just act! That’s exactly what we wanted in our animations. So instead of just smooth interpolation, we push a pose-to-pose style, adding hand-drawn poses whenever they are needed.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/169b4230161d5218c2bb5204c1c9d9619bfa9498.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/ddb9bc86259d3b3f826538dcef61120a1cc02991.gif"][/img][/p][h1]Our next steps[/h1][p]There’s still lots to do before the art direction is complete (is it ever truly finished?), but we finally feel like the foundation is solid and unique enough to build on with confidence.[/p][p][/p][p]Our next big step will be tackling new key art and an improved logo to better showcase the updated game design and new visual direction. And that’s it for this week! By now, you should be up to date with the core concepts of Don’t Kill Them All. We’d love to hear your thoughts, so please like or comment on this Journal. From here on, Journals will be monthly, covering the latest improvements to the game along with exclusive Fika news. There’s still plenty left to share![/p][p][/p][p]Remember: [b]Don’t Kill Them All![/b][/p]

notes.title: Warchief Journal #4
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/131c20eedb3b2e31d75cd807f4024e7ed86d615a.png"][/img][/p][p]This week, we’re not fooling around. The Camp is our main focus, and it’s the final piece to present before wrapping up the changes to the gameplay loop. [/p][p][/p][h1]The Camp[/h1][p]Across the lands, few places inspire as much fear as the Orc Camp. For the Orcs, that makes it the one place they can truly relax, secure in the knowledge that no enemy would dare interrupt their mud baths.[/p][p][/p][p] In Camp, you’ll be able to interact with your Orcs and help them grow. This includes crafting items, uncovering passions, and witnessing bonds of friendship (or rivalry) form between them. NPCs may also stop by to trade resources, provide station or decoration blueprints, or simply for a chat.[/p][p][/p][p][b]But before all that, we need to visit the Warlord at his throne.[/b] [/p][p][/p][h2]The Warlord’s Throne[/h2][p]As mentioned in Journal #1, your first duty as Warchief is to repair the Throne. This spot will be a central point in the Camp, as it’s where much of your story progression will take place.[/p][p][/p][p][i]"Once the player repairs the throne, the Warlord imparts a bit of knowledge onto his Warchief: Behind him lies the base of Orgon's Greatshield, an artifact fractured and lost to time, but one that the Warlord wishes to rebuild. The Greatshield is said to carry lost knowledge of the Orc civilization that could help them prosper once again. Your job is simple: scour the land and find the missing pieces of the Greatshield to bring glory to the Orcs."[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Your Warlord is convinced that this artifact is key to the return of the Orc's glory days and only imparts this knowledge upon you when he deems you worthy. This moment marks the beginning of your quest through the history of the Orcs, as well as the land they inhabit. What secrets will you uncover, what kind of leader will you be?[/p][p][/p][p][b]Time holds the answer.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/23d6b413fe7e92dcdeb3b28e834e2214333a9202.gif"][/img][/p][h2]Day-night cycle[/h2][p]Orcs have a broad metric for calculating time, which they innovatively call: Orc Hours. [b]In DKTA, most actions cost Orc Hours![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Here’s an example. At sunrise, you may begin the day with 8 Orc Hours. Cooking a meat skewer costs 2. Feel like raiding? That’ll take 4. Then you’ll have 2 to wrap up your day at camp, maybe by crafting a new station![/p][p][/p][p]When all your Orc Hours are spent, [b]it’s time to head to your tent and rest for the night.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Many factors can influence your Orc Hour consumption, like the passion of your Orc, station upgrades, or NPC actions. If you want to make the most out of every day, you’ll need to learn to juggle all these and create your own orcish production empire.[/p][p][/p][p]Raids are an essential part of the game, but some days you may just want to stay at camp, and that’s fine. The opposite is also true: if you have enough Orc Hours to raid twice in one day, go for it![/p][p][/p][p]Now that we’ve covered how to use your time to grow your clan, let’s look at how stations turn Orc Hours into results.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/3d0188ed641eebc8221f60c18099aa6225574d7a.png"][/img][/p][h2]Stations[/h2][p][i]"Orcs have their own temperament and behavior that dictate how they act. You’ll have to shape their Moods and Traits as well as enhance their Mindfulness to maximize their potential. This is achieved through Stations, which are structures that you and your Orcs can interact with to provide helpful bonuses during Raids."[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Some stations work to enhance your Orcs in specific ways. You’ll choose a station recipe based on its effect and cost, select the participants who will benefit from it, and then your operator will create the recipe.[/p][list][*][p]Put on a magic show for your Orcs to put them in a good mood before the upcoming encounter.[/p][/*][*][p]Heal an Orc’s rage by running them a nice mud bath.[/p][/*][/list][p] Others may provide a piece of equipment or even an item. These don’t require participants; however, they may still need an operator and resources.[/p][p][/p][p]Make sure to upgrade your stations! More advanced stations give you access to greater recipes, only available to Orcs who are more advanced in their passions. You can also craft, discover, or purchase station blueprints.[/p][p][/p][p][b]One small thing: the Orcs wouldn’t be broke if stations were free to use![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Recipes and Stations cost resources and Orc hours, so when you’re short on materials but know what you want to do or build next, it’s time to raid again.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/5e6e19f64475e4e8a638573cdb04a20fb32aa0e7.png"][/img][/p][h2]Building at Camp[/h2][p]What’s a base-building strategy game without camp customization? We’ll never know, because we’ve got it![/p][p][/p][p][i]"You'll want to feel at home and create a space that is truly yours. While decorating your Camp is entirely optional, if that's all you wish to do for an entire play session, you should be able to enjoy it to the fullest!"[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Building is your gateway to bringing your camp to life. By creating and upgrading stations, you’ll shape the strength of your clan. You can even improve mandatory stations, like the Warchief’s tent or the Throne.[/p][p][/p][p]Through raids and other activities, you’ll also discover blueprints for purely cosmetic structures that you can place wherever you like.[/p][list][*][p]Found a giant tooth that deserves to be shown off to the Orcs? Go ahead and display it![/p][/*][*][p]You want paths made of enemy skulls? Weird flex, but ok…[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Each construction has a cost, so manage your resources wisely![/b][/p][p][/p][p]And that’s it! It took 4 Warchief Journals, but we’ve completed a full pass on the gameplay loop of Don’t Kill Them All. Thanks for sticking with us this far! Next week’s journal will dive into [b]Art Direction.[/b] After that, the Journals will shift to a monthly schedule, giving everyone a chance to catch their breath.[/p][p][/p][p]Remember: [b]Don’t Kill Them All![/b][/p]

notes.title: Warchief Journal #3
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/28d76e0b9446be00f14f8f3395fd55a66caddbf4.png"][/img][/p][h1]Raids, Combats, and…[/h1][p]Now that we’ve covered the "[i]Why[/i]" (leading the Orcs out of misery) and the "[i]Who[/i]" (the Orcs), let’s tackle the "[i]What[/i]" (looting everything that’s left standing) and some "[i]Hows[/i]"![/p][p][/p][p align="justify"][i]"Before picking a destination, knowing what resources are available, what enemies you'll face, and what special events are occurring are all important aspects that will help you thrive. Thankfully, the more you explore regions, the more the map will reveal itself to you."[/i][/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]Time was only hinted at during the campaign, without much explanation. Now, after a year of development, we’re ready to present [b]The Warchief Journal[/b].[/p][p][/p][h2]The Warchief Journal[/h2][p align="justify"]Yes, it’s more than just a medium for Kickstarter updates: it’s also a useful in-game tool! I can’t reveal every detail just yet, but what matters for this Journal is that you’ll be able to plan your days with it.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]Each day brings unique opportunities for the Orcs, and it will be up to you to decide which ones to pursue. They vary from recurring events you can plan around to unique quests that you’ll want to drop everything to pursue. You won’t be able to do everything, so choose wisely![/p][p][/p][h3] Unique Quests[/h3][p]As the days pass, unique quests will unfold. Some will be essential to your main mission, while others will be entirely optional. Your Warlord will often happily impose several on you, but you’ll also find that NPCs and even your Orcs will occasionally require your assistance.[/p][list][*][p]Have you discovered the soul of a traveler, captured by the undying hag and sealed in a jar? Return the soul for a big reward or set it free for some Good Karma![/p][/*][*][p]A friendly merchant has been spotted in the Moldmire Bog, about to be sacrificed by a group of zealots? You might want to save him to gain access to the merchant’s guild! Or you could always take out the zealots and loot whatever’s left.[/p][/*][*][p]The Warlord wants you to lead the Orcs out of misery? It might take your whole playthrough to succeed this one![/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Situations and Interactions[/h3][p]Random interactions are not unique or recurring, but they can be predicted. As you grow familiar with your clan, you’ll learn what can trigger them and when they are likely to occur.[/p][list][*][p]Has an Orc formed a bond with another? Take them into battle and see how their teamwork makes them shine.[/p][/*][*][p]Two of your favorite Orcs are fighting: you might need to pick a side.[/p][/*][*][p]One of your Orcs woke up angry? Might want to take them to the theater and cheer them up.[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]It’s boar mating season! There is a 50% higher chance of finding them in raids![/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]Did your Orcs Kill Them All in Fablewood Thickets? The forest needs some time to recover: you’ll find 20% fewer resources there for the next couple of days.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Calendar Events[/h3][p]An Orc year is divided into four seasons, each consisting of four weeks and five days. Events are pretty straightforward: they are visible on your calendar or will unlock as you progress through the story.[/p][list][*][p]It’s Wednesday afternoon, you can be sure the Trader will be at camp.[/p][/*][*][p]It’s Burk’s birthday! What kind of gift would they like?[/p][/*][*][p]Friday raids are mandatory to end the week on a high note. Participating in a raid applies a Happy Mood to all selected Orcs.[/p][/*][*][p]Mondays mean tribute day! Be ready to hand over some of your loot to the Warlord, and let’s hope your raids were profitable.[/p][/*][/list][p]Some events can be ignored if your goals aren’t aligned, while others can seriously mess up your plans. Prioritize and strategize around them to support your clan’s growth.[/p][p] Now that we understand how time brings quests, interactions, and events, it’s time to explore one of the key playgrounds for tackling them: T[b]he Raids.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/9a4ddf19f48dca639f28a7a623363b1945a58b35.png"][/img][/p][h2]Raids[/h2][p align="justify"][i]"In order to gather resources, you must embark on daring Raids! You need 12 spiderwebs to craft a sewing Station? Better head to the forest and hunt some spiders! It's important to be strategic in your selection of Orcs for this next adventure." [/i][/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]This is what was presented during the Kickstarter campaign, and apart from expanding the range of Camp activities, it’s exactly what we’re developing.[/p][h3]
Environments[/h3][p align="justify"][i]"In Raids, you are dropped in procedurally generated environments where you can freely explore with your party and stumble upon strange NPCs, lost treasures, secrets, and deadly foes."[/i]
[/p][p align="justify"]This is still the case! After forming your raid crew, you’ll select your path on the war map. Each environment has its own special twist, rooted in its lore, revealed through gameplay.[/p][list][*][p align="justify"]Unique resources? Yes.[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]Unique enemies? Of course![/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]Unique events? You bet![/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]And more![/p][/*][/list][p]Your destination is chosen? Perfect! [b]You’ve traveled and are now ready to begin the raid![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Since the concept of [i]"Rage"[/i] was covered in Journal #2, we can now dive straight into how combat has evolved.[/p][p][/p][h2]Combats[/h2][p align="justify"]All the concepts presented under the [i]"Mindful Turn-Based Combat"[/i] section on our Kickstarter page still stand, apart from the action-based energy system. If it’s not fresh in your memory, I encourage you to revisit that section!
[/p][p align="justify"][i]"Actions are no longer tied to an energy cost. Instead, if it’s the first time an Orc uses an action, it is free. If that action doesn’t have a cooldown or a pre-determined number of uses, the Orc has the possibility of re-using it any number of times they want. The twist: each time an action is re-used, the KTA-o-meter goes up."[/i][/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]Let’s see how this statement made in Journal #2 applies to both existing and new combat systems.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/fdf99d56c582bc6520a2d108e9cf97755440ea49.gif"][/img][/p][h3]
Movements[/h3][p align="justify"]Movement isn’t only for chasing or escaping enemies, it’s also crucial for positioning your Orcs so their actions or items apply their effect patterns effectively. What’s effective is for you to decide![/p][p][/p][h3]Actions[/h3][p align="justify"]During your turn, Orcs can perform actions. Some are cooldown-based, while others affect Rage. The availability of which ones depends on their equipment, weapons, as well as their traits, moods, passions, and items. Here are a few important ones:[/p][list][*][p align="justify"][b]Basic attack:[/b] An Orc’s weapon determines the pattern and strength of the action they can perform.[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"][b]Jump:[/b] When an Orc is blocked, they can perform a jump to get past obstacles.[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"][b]Push:[/b] Want to reposition a living being? Use this action to push it forward.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Pull:[/b] Like Push, but in reverse. This action brings a living being toward an Orc.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Items[/h3][p align="justify"]Items are equipped at camp based on your Orcs’ capacity (see Journal #2). They add actions to your Orcs with a specific number of uses, depending on how many of that item are in your loadout.[/p][list][*][p align="justify"]Want to drink three chamomile teas in a row? Hurray! Your Orc is now free of Rage (and definitely a bit bloated)![/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]Need to strike an unreachable enemy, then calm down? Eat a Spicy Pepper (+1 rage), gain +3 movement with the Coffee Beans, move to the enemy, attack, and drink a Chamomile Tea (-1 Rage).[/p][/*][/list][p align="justify"][b]Unlike movement, actions can’t be undone, so be careful with your choices![/b][/p][h3]
Conflict resolution[/h3][p]In most cases, encounters will revolve solely around "[i]neutralizing all hostiles[/i]". As waves of enemies emerge, you might need to concentrate on what’s best to apply.[/p][p][/p][p][b]This is important:[/b] [b]While your Orcs have Rage, enemies have health![/b] [/p][p]Enemies reduced to 1 HP are considered defeated and will likely attempt to flee on their next turn. You can choose to kill, capture, or spare them, whatever your heart desires.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/90704d07ca49c15394651f79b5b924e89b9d7fb4.png"][/img][/p][h3]Exploration[/h3][p]It may come as a surprise, but raids aren’t just about gathering resources! Sometimes, NPCs will appear, secrets will unfold, and lost treasures will be found.[/p][list][*][p]A broken tower lies before you? Use some of your gathered resources to restore it and uncover its function![/p][/*][*][p]You found a fishing pond? Please: try our fishing mini-game![/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Raid extraction[/h2][p align="justify"]Got everything you came for? With your Orcs rage-filled and about to scream [i]"[b]KILL THEM ALL![/b]"[/i], extraction might be the smartest move!
[/p][p align="justify"]Raiding comes with risk, and the further you advance, the higher the stakes become. As you progress, you’ll unlock paths to more challenging sections of the map. While these zones offer greater rewards, they also harbor stronger enemies.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]When you’re ready to extract, return to your caravan and confirm the extraction.
[/p][p align="justify"]And bam! you’ve successfully extracted from your raid. Let’s wrap up here and get ready for the next journal, where we’ll dive into a much-anticipated topic: [b]The Camp[/b]. Instead of next week, this journal will come out in two weeks. Crafting them takes time, and we want to ensure they aren’t rushed.
[/p][p align="justify"]Remember: [b]Don’t Kill Them All![/b][/p]

notes.title: Warchief Journal #2
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/9abdf2fd1849a7f7713c79c35998b1849b8ff85b.png"][/img][/p][h1]What’s an Orc?[/h1][p]If you remember from last week's synopsis: 
[/p][p][i]"The Orcs have a mantra: 'Kill Them All!'. This battlecry strikes fear into the hearts of all who hear it as what proceeds is a mindless rampage of destruction and mayhem which leaves nothing standing in its wake."[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Your goal is to acquire resources when going on raids.[b] If all your Orcs shout [i]“KILL THEM ALL!”[/i], you lose the raid along with the resources you’ve accumulated.[/b] But how do we know when they’ll do it, and how do we prevent them from yelling it?[/p][p][/p][p]Cue the [i]"Kill Them All-o-meter"[/i]![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/57abad7e460d116678928a06a15f39702315be9c.png"][/img][/p][h1]Kill Them All-o-meter[/h1][p]The KTA-o-meter is a visual indicator of how much rage an Orc can accumulate before reaching the point of shouting [i][b]"KILL THEM ALL!"[/b][/i]. It is the same as [i]"blowing a fuse"[/i] for us Humans. There are several ways to interact with the meter, and here are some examples: [/p][list][*][p]When an Orc is hit, it increases![/p][/*][*][p]When an Orc drinks a soothing chamomile tea, it decreases![/p][/*][*][p]When an Orc sees a resource being destroyed, it increases![/p][/*][*][p]When an Orc does Yoga poses, it will freeze the next time the Orc is to gain rage![/p][/*][/list][p]Each Orc possesses an individual KTA-o-meter. When it fills completely, the Orc will unleash a [i][b]"KILL THEM ALL!"[/b][/i] shout and enter a berserk state. While still active in battle, they become uncontrollable.[/p][p][/p][p][b]They're blinded by rage, and their only desire is to destroy everything.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Don’t worry, you can still finish the fight! If you win, the Orc will come back under your control, but their KTA-o-meter doesn’t completely reset, so another shout could happen at any moment.[/p][p][/p][p]If all of your Orcs shout [i][b]"KILL THEM ALL!"[/b][/i] during the same battle, [b]your raid is lost[/b]. You will return to your camp, and live the consequences of facing your Warlord empty-handed.[/p][p][/p][p]In the end, this mechanic serves as an improvement for the Orcs’ [i]"Motivation"[/i] system, first introduced in the Kickstarter Campaign. Back then, losing all motivation meant an Orc became depressed and stopped fighting, which was essentially just a reskin of a standard [i]"Life"[/i] mechanic.[/p][p][/p][p]This isn’t your typical strategy game where units just lose health until they drop. [b]Orcs don’t die so easily![/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/c9c0af7236549407d80cf5379a43f079403697e1.png"][/img][/p][h1]The Character sheet[/h1][p]In the Kickstarter campaign, we introduced the character sheet. As you’ve seen with the KTA-o-meter and the new concept of rage, we’ve made some changes to improve the game. Some statistics got a fresh makeover, while others stayed the same.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Here’s all of them, with how they were described in the campaign and how they’ve been updated.[/b][/p][p][/p][h2]Stubbornness[/h2][p][i]‘’The more an Orc is used in combat, the higher its Stubbornness can climb. Stubbornness is added to the base energy cost of your actions.’’[/i][/p][p][/p][p]This will be explored further in Journal #3, but here’s the key change: [b]actions are no longer tied to an energy cost[/b]. Instead, if it’s the first time an Orc uses an action, it is free. If that action doesn’t have a cooldown or a pre-determined number of uses, the Orc has the possibility of re-using it any number of times they want.[/p][p][/p][p][b]The twist: each time an action is re-used, the KTA-o-meter goes up.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]It is a strategy game, after all! Will you push your units to their limits to save valuable resources and defeat your enemies?[/p][p][/p][h2]Equipment[/h2][p]This concept wasn’t explored much during the campaign, but it is an important one. Each Orc can equip one body armor, one head armor and one weapon. These provide bonuses to various statistics and can determine new actions an Orc can perform.[/p][p][/p][p]This is a good moment to expand on the KTA-o-meter and explain that rage is not purely negative. [b]Equipment can grant extra bonuses based on how much Rage an Orc has accumulated.[/b][/p][list][*][p]When Krunk wears a winged helmet, filling their Rage to the maximum grants them +3 movement. You’ll have a very mobile killing machine on your hands![/p][/*][*][p]If Snorl gains more than 3 Rage in a single encounter, they’ll break out of their chain-garb and do heavy damage to anyone in the vicinity![/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/425a616d1fdced2d053e85f7050902f1145c6b6a.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Capacity[/h2][p][i]‘’Despite the idea that bringing trinkets and tools into battle is a novel concept to Orcs, their enormous strength makes them well-suited for the job! Capacity dictates how many consumable items an Orc can carry.’’[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Items vary in size, and an Orc’s capacity dictates how many they can carry. For instance, chamomile tea requires 1 space, while a croissant requires 4. An Orc with a capacity of 6 could bring 2 chamomile teas and 1 croissant to battle, or 6 chamomile teas. This system remains unchanged![/p][p][/p][h2]Movement[/h2][p][i]‘’Evidently, Movement represents the total number of tiles an Orc can move per turn.’’[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Well, no need to reinvent movement in strategy games! This one stays the same![/p][p][/p][h2]Traits[/h2][p][i]‘’Each Orc has semi-permanent effects known as Traits. They can provide a bonus or penalty, sometimes both. Traits are discovered as you play and can be unearthed by examining an Orc's response to certain situations. If they refuse to go swimming, they may fear water. If they go into shock when they see a spider, they must be arachnophobic.’’[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Here, we’re still deciding whether Orcs should begin with discoverable traits already bound to them, or if traits should instead emerge over time as you play, shaped by the events of your sessions. [b]What do you think?[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Overall, traits still function the same way: they may grant a bonus, a penalty, or sometimes both.[/p][p][/p][h2]Bonds[/h2][p][i]‘’Orcs can develop connections between each other that help them work together in combat. This is achieved by doing actions that synergize, taking Orcs on Raids together or through special occurrences at Camp.’’[/i][/p][p][/p][p]This is cool. It stays![/p][p][/p][h2]Passions[/h2][p][i]‘’Passions are represented by skill trees where you must properly allocate points in useful actions and passives. Progression follows a linear path, requiring careful consideration for optimal builds.’’[/i][/p][p][/p][p]This is where mindfulness plays a major role! We’ll cover Stations in Journal #4, but know that there will be multiple ways to nurture your Orcs through their passions.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/e40daa34efe291a399706a537f337c8c6f643730.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Moods[/h2][p][i]‘’Moods offer powerful temporary bonuses and penalties.They are always subject to change according to the situation and can heavily alter your strategy on the fly.’’[/i][/p][p][/p][p]At the time of the campaign, our intention was for moods to function like classic status effects such as Burning, Electrified, Poisoned, or Stunned. However, because those concepts are already so familiar, we realized it was harder than expected for players to grasp how Moods influenced battles. Also, since enemies and Orcs function fundamentally differently (one is influenced by rage and the other by health), we found that adapting moods to both concepts made it cumbersome.[/p][p][/p][p][b]That’s why we decided to split the concepts and include traditional status effects in addition to Moods.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]So what are moods? They are day-based modifiers, unaffected by enemies or allies in combat. At the start of each new day, Orcs may lose, gain, or switch moods. You can also attempt to influence an Orc’s mood at camp by interacting with them, having them participate in stations, and loads of other different ways![/p][list][*][p]Is Paprika sad because their best friend stole their axe? Give them a new one to be proud of![/p][/*][*][p]Rolf started the day in a bad mood and is angry? Send them to the spa to calm down![/p][/*][*][p]Bigarock is scared because you brought them to the Forsaken Mines? This one’s on you, you evil Warchief![/p][/*][/list][p]These journals are meant to track the evolution of the game from the Kickstarter campaign to where it stands now. For that reason, I haven’t explored in depth the statistics that stayed the same. [b]Rest assured: we’ll cover them in future journals![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Coming next week: We’ll take a closer look at [b]Raids[/b], [b]Events[/b], and how [b]Time[/b] itself impacts your decisions![/p][p][/p][p]Remember: [b]Don’t Kill Them All![/b][/p]

notes.title: Warchief Journal #1
notes.notes:
[p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/b9ffc4373abbb6618dccce2d206cf40833ec4510.png"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]So here we are: our first ever journal, for future Warchiefs like yourselves![/p][p][/p][p]Yep… this was originally meant to be a journal about the art style, but as I wrote it, we realized we needed to explain all the other changes first. So now, the art style journal will be the fourth one. It’ll be worth the wait, trust us![/p][h2]
The old premise[/h2][p]If you remember correctly, here’s what Don’t Kill Them All is all about: [/p][p][/p][p][i]"Don't Kill Them All is a turn-based strategy and base-building game in which you teach bloodthirsty Orcs to develop mindfulness by discovering passions, navigating emotions, and developing healthy relationships."[/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Or is it?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]While mindfulness is a core mechanic of the game, we noticed it didn’t connect with some players in the way we’d hoped. Who would have thought that [i]"finding solutions to emotional problems"[/i] might not sound fun? Of course, that’s not how we actually describe the game! But that’s how some players saw it, and [b]first impressions really do matter.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]To all the [i]Sims[/i] fans, imagine if the game were pitched as [i]"Enjoy going to work and cleaning your house!"[/i]. Would you buy it? Probably not! Games should be an escape after a tough day, not a replay of it![/p][p][/p][p]Mindfulness is a key part of our gameplay, but making it the main focus just doesn’t work. That leads us to the big question: [b]What’s the true premise of our game?[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/180ed110be70ad16f1ffbb4bb2b4b59c5c4e441c.png"][/img][/p][h2]Synopsis[/h2][p]To better understand the new premise, here’s a little bit of DKTA's story.[/p][p][/p][p][i]"The Orcs have a mantra: 'Kill Them All!'. This battlecry strikes fear into the hearts of all who hear it, as what proceeds is a mindless rampage of destruction and mayhem which leaves nothing standing in its wake.[/i][/p][p][i]Unfortunately, this has spelled ruin for the Orc clan, as any resource that could have been collected and used to enhance their camp during their rampage was destroyed. The current Warchief is unable to bring their Orcs in raids without triggering a 'Kill Them All!'. So Urdorok, the Orc Warlord, decides new blood is needed.[/i][/p][p][i]He promotes the player, a simple Orc, to Warchief, and as their first task, they are given very clear instructions: rebuild the Warlord's Throne, which has been broken for ages, and remember: 'Don't Kill Them All!"[/i][/p][p][/p][p]We believe players need to understand [b]what[/b] they are doing and [b]why[/b] they are doing it to truly resonate with a game. For us, the [i]"What"[/i] is collecting resources, and the [i]"Why"[/i] is rebuilding the Orc clan.[/p][p][/p][p][b]In fact, both the "[i]What[/i]" and the "[i]Why[/i]" are the heart of your main quest and are central to the core gameplay loop in Don’t Kill Them All![/b][/p][p][/p][p]So, where does [i]"developing mindfulness"[/i] fit into all of this? It’s actually a [i]"How"[/i]. Connecting with a [i]"How"[/i] is often challenging, since everyone wants to bring their own unique perspective and methods to life. This is even more true in video games![/p][p][/p][p]Once we understood this, it was obvious that our premise needed to be clearer for players, especially when it came to our [i][b]"Why"[/b][/i].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/6870d9fe8304696913ee2e3181ab6647e8fcac66.png"][/img][/p][h2][i]"He promotes the player, a simple Orc, to Warchief"[/i][/h2][p]Wait, did I read that right? Isn’t Olive supposed to be promoted to Warchief in this game?[/p][p][/p][p]Yes! But as development progressed, we realized just how much fun creating your own orc really is. We enjoyed it so much that [b]we decided to let players step into the role of Warchief as themselves![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Good news: If you’ve pledged at the Archaeologist tier or above, you’ll get to play as your orc-self! We’re really excited about the customization system and hope to make it possible for players to share their Orcs’ designs with friends and family in the future.[/p][p][/p][p][b]About Olive.[/b] To be honest, we were never completely convinced by the idea of her being an outsider, and calling her an official [i]"Life coach"[/i] always made the story feel more complicated than it really is. The Orcs should be the ones to tackle their own problems, [b]and that’s it[/b]. So we’ve decided she’s no longer a relevant part of the story.[/p][p][/p][p]Don’t worry, [b]Olive isn’t entirely out of the picture![/b] She’ll still play a role in the game and help you in her own unique way. How exactly? We haven’t fully decided yet, so feel free to share your wildest ideas![/p][p][/p][p]As for the Life coach outfits unlocked by backers, rest assured, they haven’t been forgotten. Since Warchiefs aren’t life coaches themselves, our aim is to enhance the Orcs’ customization system, so everyone can look forward to something exciting. We’ll share more details about this in the future![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/d4a1ffd473ddf9cd476f623c72bcc12a98b9800a.png"][/img][/p][h2]The new premise[/h2][p]Having covered what we’ve learned about the game, here’s the fresh new premise:[/p][p][/p][p][i]"The Orcs are broke! Embody their Warchief and lead them out of misery in this brutish strategy and base-building game, where whatever’s left standing gets looted. Forge bonds between units, shape their personalities and passions, and unleash their true potential both in and out of battle."[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Here, we’re highlighting what players will actually do and feel in the game: [b]Strategically questionable, yet undeniably satisfying destruction![/b] The [i]"Why"[/i] is leading the Orcs out of misery, while the [i]"What"[/i] is looting everything that’s left standing.[/p][p][/p][h3][u][b]The "How" is up to you.[/b][/u][/h3][p][/p][p]This is where moving mindfulness out of the spotlight truly stands out. Previously, it was the only solution. Now, it’s just [b]one among many[/b], and the way you balance them will shape your Orc clan’s unique identity![/p][list][*][p]Gurd’s constantly afraid when venturing into the dark and gloomy Forgotten Mines? Help him vanquish his fear of the dark![/p][/*][*][p]Don’t feel like connecting with your troops? That’s okay. After all, fear can be an effective motivator![/p][/*][*][p]Got a bunch of jealous Orcs that haven’t been on a raid in a long time? Spread the wealth among them to keep the peace![/p][/*][*][p]Got an Orc who’s wreaking havoc on the battlefield? Alter their loadout to favor precise destruction![/p][/*][/list][p]As we said last week, this is just the beginning of our efforts to be more transparent. Don’t hesitate to ask questions or let us know how you’d like us to share updates going forward![/p][p][/p][p][b]And that’s a wrap for Journal #1! Next week, we’ll take a closer look at the Orcs and what makes them unique![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Don’t forget: Don’t Kill Them All![/p]

notes.title: It's time to update the fans!
notes.notes:
[p]Hello fellow Warchiefs![/p][p] [/p][p]Today’s a good day! I’ll be speaking on behalf of the studio, but first, let me introduce myself: I’m Francis, the new community manager at Fika. As one of the studio’s co-founders, I’ve been part of Fika since we started back in 2018. If you’ve played Ship of Fools (our first game), you’ve definitely seen my work, from editing trailers to crafting islands and combat encounters across the seas.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/644b8d61150d25c497164e18a305921fb7e7dbf9.png"][/img][/p][p]My goal is to bring more transparency between Fika and you, the fans. There was some oversight on our end in the past years, and I am currently working on ways to improve all our channels of communication, including Steam. Since the campaign ended, we’ve kept things pretty secretive about the game’s progress. There have been lots of small positive changes since what was first shown, and it’s time to get you up to speed![/p][p] [/p][p]To avoid overwhelming you with a giant, headache-inducing update, we’ll be rolling out news in weekly ‘Warchief Journals’ for the next four weeks. This way, we can chat about each change together and collect your thoughts for the team. We’ll start with the art style, then move on to the game’s story, mechanics around orcs, and finally, the general gameplay loop.[/p][p] [/p][p]Because it’s our first time adopting a more transparent communication style, we’ll begin by sharing updates in the exclusive Kickstarter Discord Channel starting next week. This way, we can fine-tune our approach before communicating it to everyone, two weeks later.[/p][p] [/p][p]So you. YES, YOU! Have you pledged on Kickstarter at the Magician tier or above? You still have time to use one of your rewards: access to the exclusive Kickstarter Discord Channel! So far, only 15% of all backers have joined us on Discord. It’s the best place to connect with the team! If you don’t have a Discord account yet, start by creating one. Then, click the link below to join our private server.[/p][p] [/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/fika-productions"]https://discord.gg/fika-productions[/url] [/p][p][/p][p]You can claim your Discord role in any channel by using the chat command "/kickstarter". You then have to enter the email address linked to your Kickstarter account. For those who have pledged for access to the private channel with the devs, you’ll gain access after redeeming your role.[/p][p][/p][p]Not interested in using Discord or unable to access the exclusive Kickstarter Discord Channel? No problem! We know Discord isn’t everyone’s cup of tea. The Warchief Journals will be posted two weeks later on our Kickstarter, our main Discord channel, and of course here on Steam.[/p][p] [/p][p]After these updates are released, we’ll shift to a monthly schedule. Each month, we’ll post a Journal that covers recent updates, changes, and what’s ahead for the game.[/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/c40478dada6fc924a628bbf9dbc8c62988d54cc7.png"][/img][/p][p]That's it! As you join our Discord and get ready for next week, enjoy this small preview of some fresh enemy designs![/p][p] [/p][p]Cheers![/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Teach orcs how to feel in Don't Kill Them All!
notes.notes:
[h2]What if we [i]Don't Kill Them All[/i][/h2]

Skulls pile up, but the coffers are empty. Blinded by their constant destructive urges, the Orcs leave nothing standing in their wake. A simple raid for wood quickly turns into a massacre and clear-cutting. Something has to change, and fast.

In Don’t Kill Them All, you assume the role of a self-proclaimed Life Coach with an extraordinary solution : What if… WE DON’T KILL THEM ALL?

[h2]A new game?[/h2]
After the success of our first game [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1286580/Ship_of_Fools/#app_reviews_hash]Ship of Fools[/url], we invite you to live a new adventure in this turn-based strategy and base-building game in which you teach bloodthirsty Orcs to develop mindfulness by discovering passions, navigating emotions, and developing healthy relationships!

[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/66192265/dont-kill-them-all?ref=18xlps][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011308/93679711e2fcafa6629fd180159d25a632bb55c7.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Kickstarter![/h2]
It would mean the world to us if you show your appreciation for our work by backing our game! You can also wishlist it now on Steam to stay in the loop. We’ve put a lot of care into it and we’re sure you’ll like it a lot!

To back our project on [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/66192265/dont-kill-them-all?ref=18xlps]Kickstarter[/url]
To watch the trailer on [url=https://youtu.be/ev5Iob6xLpE]Youtube[/url]

And remember: DON’T KILL THEM ALL
